007import javax.script.ScriptEngine;
008import javax.script.ScriptEngineManager;
009import javax.script.ScriptException;
010
011import junit.framework.TestCase;
012
013/**
014 * Test to verify that GraalJS ScriptEngine instances release memory when closed,
015 * and to check whether ScriptEngineManager shares underlying engines.
016 *
017 * <p>Run with: -Xmx512m to make OOM failures visible sooner.
018 */
019public class GraalvmMemoryLeakTest extends TestCase {
020
021    /**
022     * Tests that creating and closing GraalJS engines does not leak memory.
023     * If close() properly releases Truffle internals, heap usage should remain stable.
024     * If it leaks, this test will eventually OOM or show unbounded growth.
025     */
026    public void testEngineCloseReleasesMemory() throws ScriptException {
027        long baselineMemory = getUsedMemory();
028        System.out.println("Baseline memory: " + (baselineMemory / 1024 / 1024) + " MB");
029
030        int iterations = 200;
031        for (int i = 0; i < iterations; i++) {
032            ScriptEngine engine = new ScriptEngineManager().getEngineByName("graal-js");
033            assertNotNull("graal-js engine not found", engine);
034            engine.put("polyglot.js.allowAllAccess", true);
035            engine.eval("var x = {a: 1, b: 'hello', c: [1,2,3]}; x.a + x.c.length;");
036
037            if (engine instanceof AutoCloseable) {
038                try {
039                    ((AutoCloseable) engine).close();
040                } catch (Exception e) {
041                    fail("Failed to close engine: " + e.getMessage());
042                }
043            } else {
044                fail("GraalJSScriptEngine does not implement AutoCloseable");
045            }
046
047            if (i % 50 == 49) {
048                System.gc();
049                long currentMemory = getUsedMemory();
050                System.out.println("After " + (i + 1) + " iterations (with close): " +
051                    (currentMemory / 1024 / 1024) + " MB (delta: +" +
052                    ((currentMemory - baselineMemory) / 1024 / 1024) + " MB)");
053            }
054        }
055
056        System.gc();
057        long finalMemory = getUsedMemory();
058        long delta = finalMemory - baselineMemory;
059        System.out.println("Final memory delta (with close): " + (delta / 1024 / 1024) + " MB");
060
061        // If close works properly, delta should be modest (under 200MB for 200 iterations)
062        assertTrue("Memory grew by " + (delta / 1024 / 1024) + " MB after " + iterations +
063            " closed engines - close() may not be releasing Truffle internals",
064            delta < 200 * 1024 * 1024);
065    }
066
067    /**
068     * Tests that creating engines WITHOUT closing leaks memory.
069     * This is the control test - it should show unbounded growth.
070     */
071    public void testEngineWithoutCloseLeaksMemory() throws ScriptException {
072        long baselineMemory = getUsedMemory();
073        System.out.println("Baseline memory (no-close test): " + (baselineMemory / 1024 / 1024) + " MB");
074
075        int iterations = 200;
076        for (int i = 0; i < iterations; i++) {
077            ScriptEngine engine = new ScriptEngineManager().getEngineByName("graal-js");
078            assertNotNull("graal-js engine not found", engine);
079            engine.put("polyglot.js.allowAllAccess", true);
080            engine.eval("var x = {a: 1, b: 'hello', c: [1,2,3]}; x.a + x.c.length;");
081            // Deliberately NOT closing the engine
082
083            if (i % 50 == 49) {
084                System.gc();
085                long currentMemory = getUsedMemory();
086                System.out.println("After " + (i + 1) + " iterations (no close): " +
087                    (currentMemory / 1024 / 1024) + " MB (delta: +" +
088                    ((currentMemory - baselineMemory) / 1024 / 1024) + " MB)");
089            }
090        }
091
092        System.gc();
093        long finalMemory = getUsedMemory();
094        long delta = finalMemory - baselineMemory;
095        System.out.println("Final memory delta (no close): " + (delta / 1024 / 1024) + " MB");
096
097        // This test documents the leak - we expect growth without close
098        System.out.println("NOTE: Growth of " + (delta / 1024 / 1024) +
099            " MB confirms that unclosed engines leak memory");
100    }
101
102    /**
103     * Tests whether ScriptEngineManager returns the same engine instance or new ones.
104     * If it reuses engines, closing one might affect others.
105     */
106    public void testEngineIdentity() {
107        ScriptEngineManager mgr = new ScriptEngineManager();
108        ScriptEngine engine1 = mgr.getEngineByName("graal-js");
109        ScriptEngine engine2 = mgr.getEngineByName("graal-js");
110
111        System.out.println("engine1: " + System.identityHashCode(engine1) + " (" + engine1.getClass().getName() + ")");
112        System.out.println("engine2: " + System.identityHashCode(engine2) + " (" + engine2.getClass().getName() + ")");
113        System.out.println("Same instance: " + (engine1 == engine2));
114
115        // Document whether instances are shared
116        if (engine1 == engine2) {
117            System.out.println("WARNING: ScriptEngineManager reuses engine instances - closing one would break others");
118        } else {
119            System.out.println("OK: ScriptEngineManager creates new engine instances each time");
120        }
121    }
122
123    /**
124     * Tests whether separately-created engines share an underlying polyglot Engine.
125     * Even if ScriptEngine instances differ, they may share a polyglot Engine
126     * which holds the code cache and shape metadata.
127     */
128    public void testSharedPolyglotEngine() throws Exception {
129        ScriptEngineManager mgr = new ScriptEngineManager();
130        ScriptEngine engine1 = mgr.getEngineByName("graal-js");
131        ScriptEngine engine2 = mgr.getEngineByName("graal-js");
132
133        // Use reflection to check if they share the same polyglot Engine
134        try {
135            java.lang.reflect.Method getPolyglotContext = engine1.getClass().getMethod("getPolyglotContext");
136            Object ctx1 = getPolyglotContext.invoke(engine1);
137            Object ctx2 = getPolyglotContext.invoke(engine2);
138
139            java.lang.reflect.Method getEngine = ctx1.getClass().getMethod("getEngine");
140            Object polyEngine1 = getEngine.invoke(ctx1);
141            Object polyEngine2 = getEngine.invoke(ctx2);
142
143            System.out.println("Polyglot Engine 1: " + System.identityHashCode(polyEngine1));
144            System.out.println("Polyglot Engine 2: " + System.identityHashCode(polyEngine2));
145            System.out.println("Shared polyglot Engine: " + (polyEngine1 == polyEngine2));
146
147            if (polyEngine1 == polyEngine2) {
148                System.out.println("IMPORTANT: Engines share a polyglot Engine - " +
149                    "compiled code and shapes accumulate in the shared Engine even after Context.close()");
150            } else {
151                System.out.println("OK: Each ScriptEngine has its own polyglot Engine - " +
152                    "close() should fully release resources");
153            }
154        } catch (NoSuchMethodException e) {
155            System.out.println("Could not reflectively access polyglot context - " + e.getMessage());
156        }
157    }
158
159    private long getUsedMemory() {
160        Runtime rt = Runtime.getRuntime();
161        return rt.totalMemory() - rt.freeMemory();
162    }
163}
